exact_statement: For unit-variance centered jointly Gaussian X,Y with correlation r in [0,1], b=sqrt(2/pi) and H(x)=sign(x)-b*x, E[H(X)H(Y)]=(2/pi)(arcsin(r)-r) lies in [0,(1-2/pi)r^3]; the upper constant is optimal at r=1.
proof_or_counterexample: Planar Gaussian angular symmetry gives E sign(X)sign(Y)=2/pi arcsin(r). Regression gives E X sign(Y)=sqrt(2/pi)r. Subtracting the rank-one projection yields the identity. Positive arcsin coefficients of degrees >=3 are bounded termwise by r^3; their sum is pi/2-1. Equality at r=1 proves optimality.
